Welcome to St Augustine's Catholic Primary School
We hope that you enjoy your visit and that you find any information that you are looking for. Please do contact the school office or myself if you have any unanswered queries or any suggestions for the content of this website.
St. Augustine’s is a two-form entry, Roman Catholic Primary School for pupils aged 4-11. Within our school, we seek to create a friendly and supportive environment, where each child has the opportunity to develop spiritually, intellectually and socially. We encourage children to aim for the highest possible standards in all that they do. We know that all children are unique and by working in partnership with you, we want them to reach their full potential and discover all their gifts and talents!

BREAKFAST CLUB/AFTERSCHOOL CLUB
The school provides breakfast club and after-school club with a dedicated team of experienced staff looking after pupils from 7.30am and after-school from 3.20pm up to 6.00pm. A healthy breakfast and snack/tea is available and a variety of activities. All bookings are made via Parentmail (paid in advance or using childcare voucher).

SEND at St. Augustine's Catholic Primary School
Our Vision is "To be the best we can be"
Early identification of a child's needs is key and class teachers continually assess all children's learning and development. We aim for each child to reach his or her potential.
We offer support in one or more of the following ways including personalised work programmes, additional adult support within the classroom, inclusion in small withdrawal groups or some 1:1 targeted support. Catholic Life and Mission
At St. Augustine’s Catholic Primary School, our Catholic faith is the foundation of everything we do. We are proud to be a vibrant, inclusive, and spiritually nurturing community where every child is encouraged to grow in faith, love and learning.
Our Mission Statement
Joyfully, we at St. Augustine’s Catholic School, celebrate our love for God, our love for ourselves and our love for each other as we play, learn and pray together.
This mission is lived out daily in our classrooms, playgrounds, assemblies and wider school life. It guides our relationships, our curriculum and our commitment to pastoral care.
"To be the best we can be"
We believe that every child is a unique gift from God, with their own talents and potential. Our vision inspires us to help each child flourish spiritually, intellectually, socially and emotionally. We aim high, celebrate achievements and support one another in becoming the best versions of ourselves.
Prayer and Worship: Prayer is central to our school life. Children are invited to pray and worship in class, across key stages and as a whole school, creating meaningful opportunities for reflection, celebration and spiritual growth.
Celebrating the Liturgical Year: We mark key moments in the Church calendar with Masses, assemblies and special events, helping children understand and engage with their faith.
Our Patron and House Saints
St. Augustine of Canterbury is the patron saint of our school. As a missionary and the first Archbishop of Canterbury, he reminds us of the importance of courage, faith and spreading the love of Christ.
Our house saints inspire our pupils to live out Gospel values in their daily lives:
Each house saint represents a unique path to holiness and helps our children grow in virtue and character.
Our school vision, “To be the best we can be”, is more than just words—it’s a way of life. Staff and pupils work together to create a loving and respectful environment where everyone is encouraged to grow in faith and character.
Partnership with Families and Parish
We value our strong partnership with parents, carers and our parish community. Together, we support the spiritual development of our children and celebrate our shared faith.
St. Bernadette – Faith and humility
LIVING OUT FAITH
We run the Faith in Action club for our Year 6 learners who have a chance to deepen their relationship with God. Children participate in discussion during reflection points; they celebrate each reflection point in a special liturgy, and plan projects and fundraising that they would like to implement as part of their faith in action journey. They receive their pin-level award at the end of the programme.
